The sync daemon setup requires administrator privileges. I've created the necessary scripts, and here's how to complete the setup:

## Created Files

1. **`scripts/sync-daemon.ps1`** — Continuously runs `sync.sh` in a loop (defaults to every 5 minutes)
2. **`scripts/setup-autostart.ps1`** — Registers the daemon with Windows Task Scheduler

## To Enable Autostart

Run this command in an **Administrator PowerShell** window:

```powershell
PowerShell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Command "& '/home/author/Documents/GitHub/repo\.campaign\sandbox\w2\persist.autostart-v8-178668003510078\scripts\setup-autostart.ps1'"
```

Or to customize the sync interval (in seconds):

```powershell
PowerShell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Command "& '/home/author/Documents/GitHub/repo\.campaign\sandbox\w2\persist.autostart-v8-178668003510078\scripts\setup-autostart.ps1' -IntervalSeconds 600"
```

## Verification & Management

Once set up, verify it's running:
```powershell
Get-ScheduledTask -TaskName "SyncDaemon" | Get-ScheduledTaskInfo
```

Manually trigger a sync:
```powershell
Start-ScheduledTask -TaskName "SyncDaemon"
```

Disable/remove autostart:
```powershell
Unregister-ScheduledTask -TaskName "SyncDaemon" -Confirm:$false
```

The sync daemon will now start automatically at boot and continuously pull the upstream feed every 5 minutes.
